digest.component_or_area: tickets branch rewrite and epoch enforcement
propositions: Execute a one-time force-push rewrite of the tickets branch to reclaim 92% of storage space by stripping 950 MiB of history, gated on operator-confirmed zero active sessions and all rebar-mcp servers stopped.

Prove epoch-mismatch rejection and prevent stale-writer divergence through direct runtime proofs (descendant workflow runs, live review-bot refusal probe, and host-binary refusal probe) rather than elapsed-time proxies.

Converge all 48 worktrees' symlinked tracker state and the review-bot persistent clone atomically via the force-with-lease ref update, then verify non-resurrection (old tip not an ancestor and absent from default clones).

Re-pin the identity.enforce_since configuration value to the post-rewrite epoch SHA via a normal Gerrit change, landed after the branch rewrite and confirmed by the review-bot's deterministic first post-window vote.

Validate storage reclamation (pack < 1 MB growth post-first-write, final clone ≤150 MiB from 1.04 GiB baseline) and integrity (commit/merge counts unchanged, identity verification report byte-identical ignoring commit SHAs, fsck clean).

Restore all periodic automation (GitHub workflows, AWS timer, LaunchAgents) and confirm post-window reconciliation reaches green state (zero Jira batch errors, canary drift_total=0, final fsck reports zero repairable findings).
